advisoryNotes: The 2025 paper is used for direct Grade VI prose-question style and three-mark subparts, not as a factual source for these later chapters.
Exact ideal-answer wording is not required; each independent rubric idea earns its mark. No spelling or grammar penalties apply.
The original copyrighted scans remain local. Short quotations in active questions are included in the prompt, so no runtime source image is required.
atomicCoverageInventory: Page 109: Roger tries to snatch Mrs Jones’s purse at about eleven o’clock at night.
Page 109: the strap breaks and the combined weight makes Roger fall backwards.
Page 109: Mrs Jones picks Roger up, shakes him and makes him return her purse.
Page 109–110: Roger apologises and asks to be released; Mrs Jones takes him home.
Page 110: Roger is about fourteen or fifteen, frail and willow-wild.
Page 110: Mrs Jones asks Roger to wash his face and leaves the door open.
Page 110: Roger looks at the door but goes to the sink instead of fleeing.
Page 110: Roger wants blue suede shoes and Mrs Jones says he could have asked.
Page 110: Mrs Jones says she too wanted things she could not get and has done things she will not tell Roger.
Page 111: Mrs Jones leaves her purse unwatched; Roger sits where she can see him because he does not want mistrust.
Page 111: she prepares lima beans, meat and cocoa for Roger.
Page 111: she avoids embarrassing personal questions and talks about her hotel beauty-shop job.
Page 111: Mrs Jones gives Roger ten dollars and warns him not to steal purses.
Page 111: Roger barely manages to say thank you and never sees her again.
Pages 109–112: inline and printed exercises test vocabulary, facts, character, trust and reference to context.
